feed.title: Arun Malik
feed.subtitle: Engineering notes on AI agents, distributed systems, and software architecture.

entry.title: The Amplification Playbook
entry.summary: A proposed trial for redesigning one workflow around AI, with explicit baselines, worker input, learning checks, and a decision to stop.

entry.title: The New Skill Premium
entry.summary: Job postings show which skills employers ask for, not what caused a wage premium. Build a development plan without mistaking either for a guarantee.

entry.title: Amplifying Creativity
entry.summary: AI suggestions can improve an individual story while making a collection of stories more alike. Quality and variety need separate tests.

entry.title: Intelligence Amplification in Code
entry.summary: AI coding tools can accelerate a bounded task and slow experienced maintainers. Measure the work you actually need to finish.

entry.title: The Cognitive Offloading Trap
entry.summary: Better assisted work and better learning are different outcomes. A classroom experiment shows why the distinction matters.

entry.title: The Great Equalizer
entry.summary: AI can narrow performance gaps on a task. That does not mean it gives novices an expert's knowledge, pay, or independence.

entry.title: The Centaur Advantage
entry.summary: Human-AI routing only helps if the router can identify a useful difference in ability. A chess experiment shows both the opportunity and the difficulty.

entry.title: The road ahead: What evidence would justify more autonomy?
entry.summary: Before removing an approval step, ask what evidence would justify the change, what the trial cannot show, and what would reverse the decision.

entry.title: Incident resolution with AI: A hypothetical reference design
entry.summary: A fictional incident workflow follows an AI-assisted rollback from alert to verified recovery, with explicit authority, handoff, and failure constraints.

entry.title: From vibe coding to verified: Practising independent diagnosis
entry.summary: A proposal for practising independent diagnosis in AI-assisted engineering, with synthetic exercises and tests of whether the learning transfers.

entry.title: What sleeper agents mean for production AI systems
entry.summary: Sleeper-agent experiments show why cleaner evaluations do not prove harmful behaviour is gone, and why production checks need independent evidence.

entry.title: Designing Decision Boundaries for AI Autonomy
entry.summary: How to turn autonomy policy into testable action conditions, using a hypothetical booking service to examine consent, reversibility, retries, and the cost of delay.

entry.title: Five Ways to Question an AI Agent's Success
entry.summary: A proposed review framework for checking an agent's diagnosis, scope, lasting outcome, downstream effects, and context freshness beyond a successful tool call.

entry.title: AI Governance Needs Shared Rules and Different Controls
entry.summary: How to keep shared AI governance rules while tailoring controls to each use, with explicit ownership, testable evidence, and reassessment when permissions change.

entry.title: When Human Oversight Pays for Itself
entry.summary: A practical cost model for human review, with a hypothetical payback calculation, sensitivity checks, and cases where oversight does not break even.

entry.title: Your AI Agent's Skills Might Be Malware
entry.summary: What the ToxicSkills audit found, what its numbers do not prove, and how to limit the damage from a compromised agent skill.

entry.title: Graduated Automation: How to Scale AI Without Losing Control
entry.summary: How a procedure earns permission to act: scoped approvals, independent checks, and withdrawing autonomy when conditions change.

entry.title: The Hidden Debt in AI-Generated Code
entry.summary: What public studies reveal about persistent code-quality issues, the limits of AI-versus-human comparisons, and reviewing architectural change.

entry.title: AI and critical thinking: What the research actually shows
entry.summary: What an EEG experiment, a knowledge-worker survey, and a perspective paper tell us about AI, critical thinking, and meaningful human oversight.

entry.title: The Amplification Thesis
entry.summary: AI can improve human work without making human-plus-AI the best option. Design for amplification, then test it against the alternatives.

entry.title: AI changes the work. Who gets the gains?
entry.summary: Automating a task can help a worker, replace their work, or create demand elsewhere. The outcome depends on how jobs and institutions change.

entry.title: Why Human-in-the-Loop is Not Optional for Production AI Agents
entry.summary: The six-pillar argument for why HITL is not a transitional compromise but a structural requirement of any production AI system.

entry.title: Decentralized Granular Access Control for Agentic AI Systems in Critical Infrastructure
entry.summary: A decentralized, multi-layered access control architecture for agentic AI in critical cloud infrastructure.

entry.title: The Case for Human-in-the-Loop in Production AI Agent Systems: A Six-Pillar Framework
entry.summary: Drawing on 53 research papers, this paper argues that HITL is a structural requirement of any production AI system.

entry.title: From Reactive to Autonomous: Evolution of AI Operations in Cloud Network Infrastructure
entry.summary: A five-generation maturity model tracing the evolution from manual troubleshooting to fully autonomous incident resolution.

entry.title: Autonomous Incident Resolution at Hyperscale: An Agentic AI Architecture for Network Operations
entry.summary: A multi-agent orchestration framework for autonomous network incident resolution with safety guarantees at cloud scale.

entry.title: MCP vs CLI: A Comparative Analysis of AI Agent Tooling Interfaces
entry.summary: CLI and MCP are not competing standards. They are complementary transport layers. Evaluates both across 14 dimensions.

entry.title: Zero Trust in Azure: Strategies for Securing Cloud Infrastructure
entry.summary: Seven practical strategies for implementing Zero Trust security in Azure, covering NSGs, Private Links, Azure Policies, AVNM, and shift-left practices.
